newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Bunds capped by 103.05, downside beckons.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Bunds capped by 103.05, downside beckons.

text.p: September Bund futures on LIFFE will likely consolidate between 103.05 and Friday's low of 102.63 on Monday, before the contract heads down in the medium term, technical analysts said.

"The bearishness that was introduced into this market last week is still there and I suggest using 103.05/25 as a sell area in this contract," said David Wood, independent technical analyst based near London.
"I wouldn't want it to go through there," he said, adding the market may even stall just below the figure at 102.90/95.
By 0700 GMT, September Bunds were down 0.18 at 102.73.
"The contract will probably try and range between 103.00 and Friday's low (at 102.63) before going lower," said Wood.
He put a small prop at 102.53, but said the bulk of the support was concentrated just above 102.00, at around 102.17.
Charts show the market hit a daily low of 102.53 on July 21. The contract spiked down to hit a low of 102.17 on July 15 and a high at that level on July 2.
"That's the main level now," said Wood. "If we can break that, it would swing the big picture trend from up to down."
Wood said while the market looked capable of reaching that level, it may not yet have the momentum to push down through it.
Analysts at Chase were slightly more optimistic on the contract. They said the Bund's inability to break trendline support on Friday had improved its short term outlook.

"For short term trading behaviour it will be important to hold 102.70 and from here it should move to 103.12," they said in a note. "A break of 103.12 takes it up to 103.25 before testing Thursday's 103.48 high."
They said a break below the key 102.70 would put 102.63 under pressure, then 102.50/43, from where the contract should bounce.
By 0718 GMT, December Euromarks were down 0.03 at 96.52.
